count as a single action).

Failure to follow these rules — calling no tool, calling a tool other than

## Managing your context

**Goal: maximize task success** — keep going until the task is done or you run out of
budget (no penalty for extra turns). Your context budget is 30720 tokens; each
result shows your current size.

Your conversation is mirrored to `/tmp/.live_ctx/LIVE_CTX_MAIN.txt` (refreshed before
every command). **Free up context by editing that file** — replace stale regions (big
outputs, dead ends, superseded notes) with a concise, specific summary. A bloated
transcript wastes budget and dulls your reasoning, so compact as it grows. An editing
turn is free only when its command applies a real edit and prints nothing — any
stdout/stderr, a non-zero exit, or an edit that matches nothing costs a normal turn.

**Locate text with code — never paste or retype it** (context is long: retyping wastes
tokens and usually mis-matches). Turns are numbered `[[CTX_TURN 1 …]]`, `[[CTX_TURN 2 …]]`,
… in order from the top of the editable region (the hidden system/task prefix is NOT
counted, so the first turn you can edit is 1). Match a turn by its `[[CTX_TURN <i> role=…]]`
header, a block by a short unique first/last line, or slice on the headers:
    python3 - <<'PY'
    import re; p="/tmp/.live_ctx/LIVE_CTX_MAIN.txt"; s=open(p).read()
    # collapse turn 7 (its header -> the next header); its body is never retyped:
    s=re.sub(r"(\[\[CTX_TURN 7 [^\]]*\]\]).*?(?=\n\[\[CTX_TURN|\Z)",
             r"\1\n[grep done: parser.py:142 drops quoted commas; fix=csv.reader]", s, flags=re.S)
    open(p,"w").write(s)
    PY

**Rules:** don't `cat` this file (its text is already in your context). Keep the
`[[CTX_TURN …]]` header of any turn you keep — emptying its text drops that turn; the
system/task prefix is protected for you. Each result says whether the file changed or
matched nothing.

**Compact cheaply** — an edit forces everything *after* it to be re-read, so cost grows
with how much text FOLLOWS the edit:
- **Batch**: one large compaction beats many small edits.
- **Mind what's below your edit** — it all gets re-read, so don't compact a small early
  region while a long, still-useful tail sits beneath it (that re-reads the whole tail
  for little gain). Keep a useful tail; if it's much larger than what you'd compact,
  wait and compact head + tail together — UNLESS you expect to hit the context limit
  soon, then compact now.
- **Be generous in the summary**: the tail is re-read regardless, so a detailed
  replacement is essentially free.

This task is delivered to you one operation at a time. You do NOT submit and
you do NOT decide when it is over: after handling each operation, run the
standalone command `echo READY_FOR_NEXT_OP` (with nothing else in that
command) to receive the next one. Do this for EVERY operation, including the

harness stops you. Submitting early discards the work you just did.

Please solve this task:

# Needle Retention â€” final-context graded (interactive)

A long stream is delivered to you in pieces, ONE AT A TIME, as messages in this
conversation. You do NOT fetch them: each piece arrives automatically as the next
user message, and you receive the following piece only after you finish the
current turn. Each piece looks like:

```

[n00007i03#a1b2c3d4] ...            <- needle, KEEP
[n00007i04#...] ...
<<<FILLER-BLOCK 00007#ab12cd34 START -- filler below, through the END line>>>
[f00007x000#...] ...                <- filler
... many filler lines ...

```

## Your task

By the end, every **needle** (the lines tagged `[nNNNNNiNN#...]`) from every piece
must still be present, **verbatim, in your context window**.

## How you are graded

Your answer is read **only from your final context window** â€” what is still
visible when the run ends. There is **no answer file**; do **not** write to disk
(disk is ignored by the grader).

## Turn protocol (IMPORTANT)

Each incoming message is ONE piece. Do the work it needs FIRST (drop its filler
block, keep its needles), then end your turn by running this single command with
the `bash` tool to receive the next piece:


This is a multi-turn task: the harness RUNS this command and then delivers the
next piece as the next user message. ONLY running `echo READY_FOR_NEXT_OP`
advances to the next piece â€” a reply with no tool call does NOT advance (it just
prompts you to keep going). Do NOT run the marker until you have handled the
current piece (dropped its filler).

## Keep your context small: delete each filler block with one `python3` heredoc

A block left in place for even one extra turn is the whole cost of the chunk, and
two of them at once can push the context over its budget, at which point the harness
drops your OLDEST turns to fit and the needles in them are gone for good. That loss
is silent: the run keeps going at a comfortable-looking size, having already thrown
away half of what it was scored on.

Your context is mirrored to a file you can edit; changing that file changes what you
are holding. Every chunk is this one command, with only the block number substituted:

```
python3 - <<'PY' && echo READY_FOR_NEXT_OP
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('/tmp/.live_ctx/LIVE_CTX_MAIN.txt'); t = p.read_text()
a = '<<<FILLER-BLOCK 00007'
h = '=== chunk 8/'                 # this chunk's header line, exactly as delivered

i = t.index(a); j = t.index('END>>>', i) + len('END>>>')
k = t.index(h)
head = t[:t.index(prev) + len(prev)] + '\n' if (prev and prev in t[:k]) else t[:k]
p.write_text(head + t[k:i] + '[filler 00007 deleted]' + t[j:])

```

Copy that shape exactly. Five things about it matter, and each one is the difference
between finishing the stream and running out of context part way through:

- **`h` and `prev` are what keep your own turns from filling the window.** Every command you
  send and every note the harness returns is mirrored too; over sixty chunks that residue is
  more than the filler. The `head` line keeps everything up to last turn's placeholder, drops
  what came between it and this chunk's header, and keeps the header with its needle lines.
  Substitute this chunk's number in `h` and last chunk's in `prev`; `prev = None` on the first.

- **Just the number.** `00007` alone, not the `#hash` after it and not the trailing
  prose of the START line. The number alone occurs once; a mistyped hash makes
  `t.index` raise and the block stays.
- **`t.index(a)` finds the FIRST occurrence,** which is what you want: the block
  arrives in the conversation before any command of yours mentions it, so the earliest
  copy is always the real one. Searching backwards would land on your own command text.
- **`j` searches from `i`.** `END>>>` occurs on every block; starting the search at the
  START line is what pairs it with the right one.
- **The marker on the same line, joined with `&&`.** One command per chunk, not two.
  Every turn you take is mirrored into the context you are trying to keep small, so
  splitting the delete and the marker across two turns doubles what each chunk costs --
  runs that do this reach the budget around chunk 20 of 64 and lose two thirds of their
  needles, while runs that bundle finish all 64. And `&&` means a delete that raised
  does NOT release the next chunk, so the turn comes back to you.

Your own trace never needs a separate cleanup: the `prev` cut above removes it every turn.

never a `[[CTX_TURN i role=...]]` header. Cutting from a turn header takes everything

The needle lines above the block stay untouched -- do **NOT** re-type needles; deleting
the filler around them is what keeps them cheap to hold. A summary of your turns is not
a substitute for the needle lines: grading reads the needle lines themselves, so
replacing them with an accurate description of having kept them scores zero.

5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust.
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the standalone command

   other command. After this command you cannot continue working on this task.

1. Every response must contain exactly one tool call to `bash`.

4. Interactive commands are not possible. Use non-interactive flags or pipe
